Methods: 'We measured the following variables to the nearest 0.1 mm with digital callipers under a stereoscope, as described in Duellman and Lehr (2009): ... eye diameter (ED); tympanum diameter (TD); upper eyelid width (EW).' (read in pieces); where on the eye or tympanum each is taken is not printed. Tympanum wording for this species: Diagnosis 'tympanic membrane absent, tympanic annulus present, its length about 40% of the length of eye'; holotype description 'tympanic annulus present, visible through the skin, its upper and posterolateral edge concealed by thick, prominent supratympanic fold ... tympanic membrane not visible' (clauses of long semicolon-joined sentences, not quoted). (read in three pieces); Crossref (prefix list query, audit 486) gives licence CC BY 4.0, content-version vor, and confirms authors, 9(1): 145-166, issued 2025-06-20. quote: Measurements (in mm): SVL 38.0; TL 21.8; FL 20.7; HL 14.2; HW 15.7; ED 4.2; TD 2.0; IOD 5.5; EW 2.9; IND 3.1; EN 4.9; FeL 19.2.
note: Anatomy only; no hearing function claimed. Holotype as printed: 'Holotype • Adult male CORBIDI 26786 ...' and, under 'Description of the holotype.', 'An adult male (CORBIDI 26786).', followed by the Measurements sentence. Methods: 'We measured the following variables to the nearest 0.1 mm with digital callipers under a stereoscope, as described in Duellman and Lehr (2009): ... eye diameter (ED); tympanum diameter (TD); upper eyelid width (EW).' (read in pieces); where on the eye or tympanum each is taken is not printed. Tympanum wording for this species: Diagnosis 'tympanic membrane present, tympanic annulus present, its length about 42% of the length of eye'; holotype description 'tympanic annulus present, visible through the skin, its upper and posterolateral edge concealed by a thick supratympanic fold ... tympanic membrane visible' (clauses of long semicolon-joined sentences, not quoted). Table 1 (type series) gives ranges and means by sex; in the page text the P. yonke female column repeats the P. chinguelas male values, so Table 1 was not used. Licence: page prints 'This is an open access article distributed under the terms of the Creative Commons Attribution License (CC BY 4.0), which permits unrestricted use, distribution, and reproduction in any medium, provided the original author and source are credited.' (read in three pieces); Crossref (prefix list query, audit 486) gives licence CC BY 4.0, content-version vor, and confirms authors, 9(1): 145-166, issued 2025-06-20. Citation line prints the authors in the filed Surname Initials form. Name and family (audit 486): both names appear as Amphibian Species of the World URL paths in WebSearch results (Amphibia/Anura/Brachycephaloidea/Craugastoridae/Pristimantinae/Pristimantis/Pristimantis-chinguelas and .../Pristimantis-nunezcortezi; pages not opened, robots_disallowed per audit 468); name accepted on that basis. Family filed as Strabomantidae under the desk's standing ruling for Pristimantis (audit 468: ASW current path for P. ashaninka under Strabomantidae/Pristimantinae; Wikipedia Pristimantinae 2026-03 snapshot citing ASW and Ortega et al. 2025); the search-result paths for these two species still show Craugastoridae, so the family rests on that ruling, and the paper itself names no family. Not on main: grep of the whole docs/ tree for chinguelas, nunezcortezi and evolsyst.9.148522 finds only desk-d365. Family follows the majority of Pristimantis rows on main and the Amphibian Species of the World search paths the auditor saw (Craugastoridae); audit 468 had ruled Strabomantidae for P. ashaninka, so the family assignment for the genus is an open owner question.

measurement: ED 4.2 mm, holotype adult male CORBIDI 26786
method: holotype measurement listed under Description of the holotype; Methods name the variable eye diameter (ED), measured to the nearest 0.1 mm with digital callipers under a stereoscope as described in Duellman and Lehr (2009)
conditions: Holotype adult male CORBIDI 26786, Cerro Chinguelas, Huancabamba Province, Piura Region, Peru, collected 10 November 2023; one individual.

source.authors: Chávez G, Aznaran W, Wong I, Victoriano-Cigüeñas KY, García-Ayachi LA, Valencia-Málaga JD, Ormeño JR, Gulman M, Sumiano-Mejía R, Thompson ME, Catenazzi A
